children: Asian spot liquefied natural gas prices on Friday eased from a near four-year high this week, as subdued northeast Asian demand and hopes for progress in US-Iran talks weighed on the market.
The average price for November delivery into northeast Asia was estimated at $25.85 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), down from $27.00/mmBtu last week.

US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said this week.

"Northeast Asia is largely covered heading into this winter," said ICIS analyst Evan Tan, noting that Japan's inventories are healthy and that any pre-winter restocking by South Korea is likely to be limited by expectations of mild weather.
China has also stayed out of the spot market as cheaper domestic gas makes LNG uneconomic, with South Asia doing most of the prompt buying, he added.

"Structural demand remains strong from Bangladesh. India is still tendering for fertiliser and city gas needs, but demand from non-subsidised sectors, like industrial and refining consumers, is seeing declines at current prices," Tan said.
Expectations of higher Qatari exports have also weighed on prices, after an increase in dark transits by QatarEnergy vessels in recent weeks, said Martin Senior, head of LNG pricing at Argus.

"Many of the firm's older carriers are now positioned near the Strait of Hormuz, or have their Automatic Identification System transponders off - both a sign that the firm could continue these transits," he said.
"This has boosted Middle East supply expectations slightly in a tight global market, though volumes are still very far away from where they were pre-March."

In Europe, S&P Global Commodity Insights assessed its daily Northwest Europe LNG price benchmark for cargoes delivered in October on an ex-ship basis at $24.795/mmBtu on Thursday, a discount of $0.395/mmBtu to the price at the Dutch TTF gas hub.
Argus assessed the October DES NWE price at $24.81/mmBtu, while Spark Commodities assessed it at $24.616/mmBtu.
"European storage inventories rose above 70% during the week, reducing immediate concerns around winter preparedness," said Aly Blakeway, head of Atlantic LNG at S&P Global Commodity Insights.

Strong LNG imports, healthy send-out rates and seasonally weak demand helped ease near-term supply concerns, leaving comfortable cargo availability across both prompt and forward delivery windows, Blakeway added.
In LNG freight, Atlantic rates rose for a fourth straight week to $29,500 a day, while Pacific rates gained for a third straight week to $31,000 a day, said Spark Commodities analyst Qasim Afghan.
The US front-month arbitrage to northeast Asia via the Cape of Good Hope is still pointing to Europe, while the Nigeria prompt arbitrage, also via the Cape, is firmly pointing to Asia, he added.

title: Asia spot prices slip on weak northeast Asia demand, US-Iran diplomacy hopes
